question: Why does the shipped cooperative-matrix qmm kernel run at ~1035 GFLOP/s at the dominant prefill cell (gate_up, 1053x896x9728) when the same matrix instruction sustains 2148 GFLOP/s (receipts/2026-09-11-fma-ceiling)? Read the generated AGX machine code, attribute the stall at instruction level, and fix the driver if the cause is there.

base.kernel: shaders/qmm_coopmat.comp (shipped, unmodified), compiled by the installed driver
base.bench_wheel: mlx_omarchy-0.32.2.dev202609110924+48ea34dd (bench arm 0 = shipped kernel; wheel kernel identical to default dispatch)

baseline_reproduction.cell: 1053x896x9728 q4 group-64 transposed, 4 warmups + 6 timed, wall perf_counter
baseline_reproduction.note: Matches receipts/2026-09-11-coopmat-ilp-chains arm0 (17.5996 ms, 1043.0, same digest) - baseline reproduced on the same day, same driver.

step_body_accounting.unit: steady-state 16-k step of the k loop, per lane, final packed AGX ISA (not NIR); one step body loops (while $r36<4 per 64-k chunk)

matrix_fmadd.verdict: no issue waste; 2 ksub-steps x (2 A frag x 4 B frag); dependency spacing 8 inside each 8-fmadd burst; ks=1 fragment loads issued mid-burst (already software-pipelined inside the math phase)

shared_load_lload.form: scalar 32-bit each; each 8x8 fragment = 2 loads per lane with adjacent 8-byte addresses (r38 and r38+4) - pairable into 12 vector loads

shared_store_lstore.form: 8 x_s (scalar f32 halves of unpacked f16x2) + 8 w_s (dequant), scalar

global_load.form: 4 x words + 1 packed w word; each inside its own divergent guard block; each followed by a wait within 2 instructions

scoreboard_wait.form: all 5 loads serialized on effectively one scoreboard: load->wait pairs, no overlap between the 4 x-word latencies

integer_address_math.breakdown: 65 iadd + 11 and + 10 shr + 8 imadd + 8 bfeil + 5 shl
integer_address_math.note: ~90 of the 107 are recomputed per step from lane-constant values (lid%8, lid/8, x_s/w_s store addresses, the 12 fragment load addresses rebuilt from thread_index_in_simdgroup, w_base) - loop-invariant work NIR CSE/LICM did not lift across the step loop boundary

float.form: 8 ffma (dequant) + 8 u32_to_f + 8 fadd (f16->f32 widening via fadd x,-0.0)

register_pressure.accumulators: r18-r33 (8 fragments x 2 f32) live in registers across the entire k loop including the staging phase - no spill, no reload

stall_attribution.cycle_math: 16 matrix ops/step at the measured 14.9 clk/op sustained rate (2148 GFLOP/s) = 240 clk matrix-pipe time per step. Measured 1046 GFLOP/s implies ~494 clk/step, so the matrix pipe idles ~half the step. Issue time of the 229-instruction body (~229 clk at 1/clk) alone cannot explain the gap; the serialized global-load waits and the block-exit drain can.
stall_attribution.primary_cause_driver: agx_insert_waits_local (src/asahi/compiler/agx_insert_waits.c) used 2 scoreboard slots and drained ALL pending messages at EVERY block exit - including exits that are exec-mask transitions, not real branches. The source batches its 4 x-word loads in a separate loop from the unpack (qmm_coopmat.comp lines 126-143); the driver re-serialized them: each guarded load sits in a then-arm whose block exit inserts a wait before the else. Result: 4 exposed global-memory latencies per step instead of ~1, plus the w-word load similarly drained.
stall_attribution.secondary_cause_driver: ~90 loop-invariant integer address ops recomputed every step (NIR local-only CSE; no cross-block/LICM lifting in the AGX pipeline for these). Bounds the win from wait-fixing alone.
stall_attribution.tertiary: 24 scalar fragment lloads that are pairwise adjacent (vectorizable to 12); minor issue-slot and shared-bandwidth effect.
not_the_cause: MulAdd issue order inside bursts (spacing 8, matches fma-ceiling shape)
barrier count (2/step is the source's single-buffered structure; driver cannot legally merge)

unified_cause_cross_reference: Tonight's four negative receipts read as one cause when viewed through the ISA: agx_insert_waits_local's per-block scoreboard draining flattens whatever parallelism the source expresses, unless a data-parallel segment happens to live in a single basic block. (1) receipts/2026-09-11-qmm-coop-datapath: operand-transport restructures (fewer/larger staging chunks) lost because the staging phase they shrank was inflated by the driver's serialized guarded loads - trading shared memory and occupancy for it bought nothing. (2) receipts/2026-09-11-coopmat-ilp-chains: every bit-preserving ILP schedule lost; that receipt named the deficit as the between-burst 'memory segment' plus 16 loop-carried MOVs - this dump resolves that segment into 5 drained loads and ~90 recomputed lane-constant address ops, neither reachable by issue-order changes inside the loop. (3) receipts/2026-09-12-prefill-fma-qualify: a scalar-FMA kernel with NO barriers and NO shared memory still reached only 545 GFLOP/s (a quarter of the scalar ceiling) - removing the barriers cannot remove driver-inserted per-block waits on its global loads; its own verdict's operand-traffic bound is this same serialization seen from the memory side. (4) receipts/2026-09-12-weight-memory-type: +6.0% paired flat-stream read gain from the uncached heap type moved no token (model deltas -1.7 to +1.0%) - the kernels are latency/issue-starved by serialized waits, not bandwidth-starved, so extra memory throughput had nothing to feed. The counter-example proves the mechanism: receipts/2026-09-12-decode-chunked-softmax batched its subgroupAdds/exps inside ONE straight-line block and landed -1.4 to -4.1% decode latency - no guarded loads, no block-exit drains in the segment, source-level ILP survived.

driver_patch.change: agx_insert_waits.c rewritten: scoreboard slots 2->4 (2-bit packed immediate), pending state carried across exec-mask fallthrough edges of divergent if/else regions with merge seeding (union of both arms), waits inserted at first use; only real branches, back-edges and barriers drain. Well-formedness guards fall back to the old conservative per-block drain on any unexpected CFG shape.
driver_patch.reproducibility: branch pushed to origin; A/B via explicit ICD JSON files, never an install over the system driver
driver_patch.named_fix_commit: hk/agx-wait-batching @ 8f3169a4342 (committed UNBUILT, UNVERIFIED, on top of WIP debug commits; first action on pickup: build, dump the shipped qmm coopmat kernel, confirm the five guard-load waits move to first use)

ab_measurement.protocol: paired interleaved, same stock driver hk6f6afc8, 3 rounds x 8 shapes, wheel 48ea34dd (shipped kernel) vs wheel 8f6de34c (uniform-load shader), 4 warmups + 30 timed medians per run; digests compared per shape

shader_restructure_result.bit_exactness: PASS - all 8 shapes, 3 rounds, f16 digests identical to shipped kernel
shader_restructure_result.verdict: NEGATIVE on the stock driver - not landed. Removing the divergent guards (the drain sites this receipt identified) made the driver's codegen WORSE at every large shape. Suspected mechanism, unverified: the per-tile hoisted arrays (xbase/xmask/xsoff) indexed by a loop variable need loop unrolling to stay in registers; without it they spill to scratch in the hot loop - the same failure mode as the 2026-09-11 forced-unroll receipt. The ISA of the new shader was not dumped before budget close; that dump is the named next step.
shader_restructure_result.conclusion: The shader-level fix Main proposed is falsified for this driver: the drain sites are real, but removing them at source level does not recover the serialized latency - the stock scheduler's placement of the straight-line loads is worse. The driver-side fix (making the pass actually fire) remains the only validated route to the headroom.

driver_patch_status.proven_on_target: NO - the frame detection never fires: zero pushes across every shader (debug print, 263 blocks examined, 88 mask branches, 0 pushes). Root cause found at close: the shape guard resolves end_then via order[else_index-1], but blocks are visited in index order, so the then arm's last block is not yet in the order array when the frame pushes - end_then compares against NULL and every frame fails.
driver_patch_status.named_fix: defer merge resolution to else-arrival (all then-arm blocks are visited by then): capture then_exit, compute merge from order[else_index-1]'s single fallthrough successor, fold then_exit into running and retire the frame if the shape is unexpected. Drop the pointer identity check on term->target in favor of index equality. ~30-line change to the committed pass; NOT yet built or verified.
driver_patch_status.evidence_patch_does_something: 4-slot change alone shifted preamble waits (stock 216 total waits vs patched 1966 across all shaders; coopmat kernel 32->38 waits, preamble drains removed) - the pass executes and changes codegen, just never through the intended frame path.
driver_patch_status.digest_screen: deliberately not run - the patch is inert on the target guards; screening a no-op proves nothing (agreed with Main).

status: ANALYSIS COMPLETE + DRIVER PATCH ROOT-CAUSED INERT + SHADER RESTRUCTURE MEASURED NEGATIVE; nothing landed as a perf change
reconciliation: The de-diverged staging result must be read precisely: it FALSIFIES the simple form of the drain theory ('remove the exec-mask block exits the driver drains at, and the serialization disappears') - removing every drain site from the staging phase made the kernel 13-26 percent slower, bit-exactly, on the stock driver. What survives is the narrower claim: the driver's wait placement costs real latency in the staging phase (the stock ISA shows five load->wait pairs the source does not ask for), but the cost is a property of how the AGX scheduler places waits and loads for a given CFG, not of the presence of block exits per se. A source-level CFG change is confounded: it also changes scheduler decisions, RA and array promotion (the de-diverged shader needs its hoisted per-tile arrays promoted to registers, which requires unrolling the backend refuses on this shape - the same cliff as the 2026-09-11 forced-unroll receipt). The two findings are consistent; neither alone identifies the dominant term.

handoff_open_questions.question: What is the actual dominant term of the 1034-vs-2148 GFLOP/s gap, given: zero issue waste, zero spills, zero-traffic ladder caps at 1459 inside the real dispatch geometry (68 percent of flat), barrier-free scalar kernel is worse (545), de-diverged staging is worse on the stock driver?

H1_dispatch_geometry_ceiling.claim: The 64-lane workgroup / 16 KiB-shared / tile-looped geometry caps the matrix pipe near 1459 regardless of kernel body; the shipped kernel is close to that cap once its own latency costs are counted.
H1_dispatch_geometry_ceiling.discriminator: Rerun the receipts/2026-09-11-fma-ceiling zero-traffic coopmat ladder with three geometry arms: 4 KiB shared skeleton (matches shipped), 128-lane workgroups (two tiles per WG), and no tile loop (flat per-tile dispatch). If 4 KiB alone recovers ~1900+, shared footprint/occupancy is the wall; if 128-lane recovers, subgroup residency is.
H1_dispatch_geometry_ceiling.instrument: Existing fma_bench.c + sweep.py harness, no mlx, one GPU window, ~20 min.

H2_wait_placement_at_barrier.claim: The scheduler sinks load waits to the barrier drain rather than first use even without block exits, so staged-load latency lands on the barrier path; the block-exit drain is one instance of a general wait-placement weakness.
H2_wait_placement_at_barrier.discriminator: Dump the de-diverged kernel (wheel 8f6de34c) with AGX_MESA_DEBUG=shaders on the stock driver and diff wait placement against the shipped kernel: if the waits sit immediately before the threadgroup_barrier instead of at first use, H2 is confirmed and the driver fix target moves from block exits to barrier-drain + scoreboard allocation.
H2_wait_placement_at_barrier.instrument: One dump run + ISA diff, ~5 min, no new build.

H3_shared_bank_aliasing.claim: w_s pitch 32 f32 cycles the full bank set on every fragment lload and staging lstore (flagged in receipts/2026-09-11-qmm-coop-datapath: upstream pads, we do not); bank-conflict serialization, not scoreboard waits, is the staging cost.
H3_shared_bank_aliasing.discriminator: Step-level padding variant: w_s[16][34], x_s[34][16] (shared layout only, arithmetic untouched, bit-preserving). The qmm-coop-datapath arm 2 padded at chunk granularity and lost; step-level 32->34 was never isolated.
H3_shared_bank_aliasing.instrument: One shader variant + kernel probe with digest gate, ~30 min including wheel build.

H4_runtime_effective_chains.claim: Even with perfect staging, the 8-fmadd bursts are too short (8 ops x ~15 clk = 120 clk) for the pipe to ramp between long idle phases, so time-averaged chains stay near 1 (the ilp-chains 1-chain rung at 1014 matches the shipped 1043).
H4_runtime_effective_chains.discriminator: A bit-preserving schedule that doubles burst length without growing shared memory: stage 32-k of A fragments in registers per subgroup (2 f32/lane each) and issue 16-fmadd bursts; digests must hold. If GFLOP/s lands near the 2-chain rung (~1360), burst length is the binding term.
H4_runtime_effective_chains.instrument: One arm on the wave/CoopmatIlpChains bench skeleton, digest-gated, ~1 h.

handoff_open_questions.order_of_attack: H2 first (5 min, pure read - it also settles whether the committed-but-unbuilt 8f3169a4342 targets the right site); then H1 (20 min, existing harness); then H3/H4 as shader arms if H1 leaves a gap unexplained.
